tweet.text:
Topic: Peer to peer agents are faster. Now give the peers identities.

Source: https://scalingintelligence.stanford.edu/pubs/delm.pdf

1/ Love this work. DeLM drops the orchestrator. Agents run side by side, share an append only log of findings and dead ends, claim work from a queue, and each one verifies its own solution. On long coding tasks it beat single harness runs on accuracy and finished up to 2x faster.

2/ The design choices are good security instincts too. An immutable log, so mistakes get corrected by new entries instead of edits. Every agent checks the original task, not a peer's summary. One container per agent. A full event trail of who posted, read, and applied what.

3/ The gap is trust between peers. Every agent believes every other agent. One injected peer can post a false finding, kill the right fix with a fake dead end, or publish a poisoned file the others apply. Append only makes tampering visible. It doesn't make it impossible.

4/ Red team: plant the injection where one agent reads it and watch it spread through the log. Seed a helper file and see who applies it. Claim the critical task and stall.

5/ Defense: sign every entry per agent, make a second peer independently confirm a finding before anyone acts on it, review diffs before apply, scan entry text for secrets, lock down egress, and mix models so one injection can't capture the whole team.

6/ Decentralized is where agent work is heading. The coordination layer is the new trust boundary. Build identity into it now, while the peers are still small.
